title: セイバールート十日目-09

pages.ja:
家に遠坂を残して、セイバーと外に出る。
朝の七時半。
坂道はひどく静かだ。
この時間、いつもは生徒たちが登校しているというのに、今日に限って人影はまばらだった。

pages.en:
Leaving Tohsaka at home, Saber and I head out.

It is half past seven in the morning.

The road down the hill is eerily quiet.

Normally it would be full of students on their way to school, but today there are only a handful of people about.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Leaving Tohsaka at home, I leave with Saber.
It’s seven thirty in the morning.
The hill is really quiet.
Students usually go to school at this time, but not many people are around today.

pages.ja:
「学校は休校だそうですね。
死者が出なかったとはいえ、大半の生徒はいまだ立ち上がれる体ではないという事ですか」
pages.jaRuby:
「学校は休校だそうですね。
死者が出なかったとはいえ、大半の生徒はいまだ立ち上がれる体ではないという事ですか」
pages.en:
“I hear the school has been closed.

“No one died, but most of the students are still in no condition even to stand.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I hear the school has closed down temporarily.
Even though nobody died, most of the students apparently cannot stand up yet.”

pages.ja: 「……重度の栄養失調みたいなもんだからな。まともに動けるようになるまで何日かはかかるだろ」
pages.jaRuby: 「……重度の栄養失調みたいなもんだからな。まともに動けるようになるまで何日かはかかるだろ」
pages.en: “…It's basically severe malnutrition. It'll probably be a few days before they can move around normally again.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…It’s like severe malnutrition, so it should take a few days before they’ll be able to move again.”

pages.ja:
だが、それは比較的軽い被害だ。
一生残る傷を負った者もいた。
pages.jaRuby:
だが、それは比較的軽い被害だ。
一生残る傷を負った者もいた。
pages.en:
And those are the relatively mild cases.

Some students suffered injuries that will stay with them for the rest of their lives.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But those are the lucky ones.
Transformation of the skin, necrosis of the tips of the limbs…
I hear there were even students on the verge of blindness.
Some of them received injuries that will last a lifetime.

pages.ja:
「……大河も病院に運ばれたと聞きます。見舞いに行かずともいいのですか、シロウ？」
「ああ、藤ねえのはただの疲労だと。心配しなくてもいいから、真面目に家で勉強してろとさ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…I heard Taiga was taken to the hospital as well. Are you certain you need not visit her, Shirou?”

“Yeah. Fuji said it was just exhaustion. Told me not to worry about her and to stay home and study for once.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I hear Taiga was taken to the hospital as well. Is it all right not to go visit her, Shirou?”
“Yeah, they said Fuji-nee’s just fatigued. They told me not to worry about it and to study at home.”

pages.ja:
出かける際、藤村の家に電話を入れて、藤ねえの無事は確かめた。
見舞いに行きたいが、今はそれだけで我慢しなくてはいけない。

pages.en:
Before we left, I called the Fujimura house and made sure Fuji was all right.

I want to visit her, but for now, that will have to be enough.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I called the Fujimura house and checked on Fuji-nee’s state before I left the house.
I would like to go visit her, but I should hold off on that for now.

pages.ja:
「では探索に専念するのですね。それはいいのですが、シロウに当てはあるのですか？
私はサーヴァントの気配を読みとれますが、それも近づかなければ判りません。何か手がかりがなければ、捜し出すのは難しいのではないでしょうか」

“Then we shall devote ourselves to the search. That is well and good, but do you have any leads, Shirou?

“I can sense another Servant's presence, but only at close range. Without some clue to guide us, finding her will be difficult.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Then you are concentrating on the search? That is fine, but do you have any guesses?
I am able to feel the presence of Servants, but that is only possible if I am near them. I believe it will be difficult to find them without some sort of a clue.”

pages.ja:
「ああ。たしかに慎二が何もせずに隠れていた場合、捜し出すのは難しいだろ。けどあいつの性格から言って、昨日の今日で大人しくしているとは思えない」
慎二はやられっ放しで黙ってるタイプじゃない。

“Yeah. If Shinji goes into hiding and does nothing, we'll have a hard time finding him. But knowing him, I can't see him lying low after what happened yesterday.”

Shinji is not the type to take a beating and let it go.

“Yeah. If Shinji was hiding and not doing anything, it would be difficult to find him. But considering his personality, I don’t think he’ll stay quiet after that incident yesterday.”
Shinji’s not the type to stop when he’s beaten.
He’s the kind of guy that’ll take revenge.

大きな建物で、人が沢山集まるところを当たっていけばいい」

pages.en:
“—You mean to search for the bounded field, rather than Rider's Master.”

“Right. We may not be able to sense a Master, but we'll notice a bounded field that large once we get close. Then we can pin down where it is.

“We just have to check the big buildings where a lot of people gather.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So we will not be looking for Rider’s Master, but for the boundary field?”
“Yeah. Even if we can’t perceive the Master, we can sense the boundary field if we get near it. And that will tell us about possible locations as well.
We just need to look for large buildings where lots of people gather.”

pages.en:
“I am impressed. Well done, Shirou.”

“I'm not always reckless, you know. I wouldn't have suggested this if I wasn't sure we could find him.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I am surprised. You are thinking pretty well, Shirou.”
“It’s
“Hey now. It’s
not like I’m not thinking, you know? I wouldn’t say something like that if I wasn’t confident about finding them.”

pages.ja:
……そう、自信はある。
結界の事もあるが、それより俺たちが歩き回る事の方に意味がある。
俺が慎二を放っておけないように、おそらくはあいつも、俺をこのまま放っておく気はないだろうから。

pages.en:
…And I am sure.

The bounded field is one reason. More important, though, is simply being seen walking around town.

Just as I cannot leave Shinji alone, he probably has no intention of leaving me alone either.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Yes, I’m confident.
There’s the matter of the boundary field, but there’s more meaning in us walking around.
Just as I can’t leave Shinji alone, I bet Shinji doesn’t intend to let us go either.

pages.ja:

セイバーにライダーの気配を読みとってもらう。

……まあ、自分の家に潜伏するほど落ち着いた男でもあるまい。

I have Saber feel for Rider's presence.

She senses nothing.

…Well, Shinji is hardly calm enough to hole up at home.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Just to be sure, we go to Shinji’s house.
I have Saber check for the presence of Rider.
The result is negative.
…Well, he’s not the kind of guy that would be resting at home.

pages.ja:
「行こう。慎二が結界を張るとしたらこっちの町じゃなくて、新都の方だ。オフィス街のビルを総当たりしていこう」

pages.jaRuby:

I call to Saber, and we leave the Matou house behind.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Let’s go. If Shinji’s going to construct a boundary field, it’ll be in Shinto, and not over here. Let’s go to each of the office buildings.”
Calling out to Saber, I leave the Matou house.

Saber is right next to me and answers as if nothing has happened.

pages.mirrorMoon: “…You’re mean. Even if it was bad for me, you should have woken me up. I told you we don’t have time to be resting.”

pages.ja:
「休息は必要な行為です。それにシロウが眠っていたのは一時間程度ですから、そう問題はないでしょう」
「む、そりゃ結果論だ。俺が起きなかったらどうするつもりだったんだよ、一体」

“Rest was necessary. Besides, you were asleep for only an hour. I see no great problem.”

“Hmph. That's hindsight. What were you going to do if I hadn't woken up?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Resting is a necessary action. And you were only sleeping for an hour, so there should be no problem.”
“Hm, that’s only in hindsight opinion. What were you going to do if I didn’t wake up?”

pages.ja: 「そうですね、あまり変わりはないでしょう。日が落ちて寒くなってきましたから、そろそろ声をかけようと思っていたところです」
pages.jaRuby: 「そうですね、あまり変わりはないでしょう。日が落ちて寒くなってきましたから、そろそろ声をかけようと思っていたところです」
pages.en: “Much the same, I imagine. The sun has set and it is growing cold, so I was just about to wake you.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Let me see, it would not have been too different. The day has ended, and it was starting to get cold, so I was about to wake you up.”

Saber answers simply.
…This is no good. No matter how I think about it, she’s right in this case.

original.ja:
あっさりとセイバーは返してくる。
……ダメだこりゃ。どう考えても、今回はセイバーの言い分のが正しいと思う。

original.en:
Saber answers without hesitation.

…No getting around it. However I look at it, she’s right this time.

pages.ja:
「……まあ、たしかに体の調子はすごくいいけど」
ベンチから立ち上がって、野原をとつとつと歩く。
野原にかつての面影はない。
住宅地だった頃の面影も、あの、赤い世界だった頃の面影も。
それなのに、ここで眠っただけでつまらない残像を見たのは、なんとなく癪に障った。

pages.en:
“…Well, I do feel a lot better.”

I rise from the bench and walk slowly across the field.

Nothing remains of what this place once was.

Nothing of the neighborhood it had been, nor of the red world it became.

Even so, it irritates me that merely sleeping here should have shown me such a pointless afterimage.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Well, I certainly do feel much better.”
I get up from the bench and start to walk through the field.
There’s no trace in the field of what came before.
No trace of when it used to be a residential district, nor any trace of when it was that red burning world.
It kind of irritates me that in spite of that, I saw that afterimage just by sleeping here.

pages.ja:
「シロウ……？ 何か問題でもあるのですか……？」
「ああ、いや。どうせ休むなら、別の場所にするべきだったなって。ここはどうも、嫌な思い出がありすぎる」
pages.jaRuby:
「シロウ……？ 何か問題でもあるのですか……？」
「ああ、いや。どうせ休むなら、別の場所にするべきだったなって。ここはどうも、嫌な思い出がありすぎる」
pages.en:
“Shirou…? Is something wrong?”

“No. I was just thinking that if I had to rest, I should've done it somewhere else. This place has too many bad memories.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Shirou…? Is there a problem…?”
“Oh, no. I just thought we should have rested somewhere else if we were going to rest. There are too many bad memories here.”

pages.ja: 「嫌な思い出……？ シロウはこの場所に縁があったのですか？」
pages.jaRuby: 「嫌な思い出……？ シロウはこの場所に縁があったのですか？」
pages.en: “Bad memories…? Do you have some connection to this place, Shirou?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Bad memories…? Do you have some connection to this place?”

pages.ja: 「え……？ そっか、話してなかったっけ。俺、昔はこのあたりに住んでたんだ。十年前の話だけどな。大きな火事が起きて、両親も家も焼け落ちた。そん時に切嗣に助けられて、そのまま養子になったんだよ」
pages.jaRuby: 「え……？ そっか、話してなかったっけ。俺、昔はこのあたりに住んでたんだ。十年前の話だけどな。大きな火事が起きて、両親も家も焼け落ちた。そん時に[ruby text=オヤジ char=2]切嗣に助けられて、そのまま養子になったんだよ」
pages.en: “What…? Oh, right. I never told you. I used to live around here. This was ten years ago. There was a huge fire, and I lost my parents and my home. My dad—Kiritsugu—saved me, and then he adopted me.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Huh…? Oh, I must’ve not told you yet. I used to live here. It’s ten years ago, though. But there was a big fire and both my parents and my house burned up. I was saved by Kiritsugu and became his foster child.”

pages.ja:

「ああ、切嗣の実の子供って訳じゃない。それに聖杯戦争と無関係って訳でもないのかな。
ここが前回の戦いの、最後の場所だってのは聞いてるよ。そこで生き残った俺がマスターになるんだから、皮肉というか、縁があるっていうか」

pages.en:
“What…? Then you—”

“Right. I'm not Kiritsugu's son by blood. And I guess I'm not completely unrelated to the Holy Grail War, either.

“I heard this was where the last war came to an end. Now the boy who survived it has become a Master himself. I don't know whether to call that irony or fate.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What…? Then you are…”
“Yeah, that means I’m not Kiritsugu’s child. And I guess I’m not completely unrelated to the Holy Grail War either.
I heard that this place was the final battleground in the last war. The one person who survived it became a Master, so I guess you could call it kind of ironic.”

あれから十年は経つというのに、ここの土は草の生えが悪いようだ。
……死んでいった人たちの無念が、この土地に染み込んでいるせいかもしれない。

We walk across the field.

Ten years have passed, yet grass still seems reluctant to grow in this soil.

…Perhaps the anguish of the dead has soaked into the earth.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I walk through the field.
It’s been ten years since that happened, but it seems this ground isn’t fertile at all.
…Maybe the regret of the dying people has seeped into this land.

“Shirou. Is that why you are so determined to prevent casualties?

“Because you yourself were a victim of the Holy Grail War, you cannot bear to let anyone else become one?”

“What—no, that's…”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Shirou. Is that why you seek to prevent any victims?
Since you are a victim of the Holy Grail War, you do not want another victim like yourself…?”
“Ehwell, that’s…”

だが、不思議とそう思った事は一度もなかった気がする。
pages.jaRuby:

Now that she says it, I suppose that would make sense.

Strangely, though, I do not think I have ever seen it that way.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Now that she mentions it, maybe that’s logical.
But strangely, I’ve never thought about it that way.

「……どうだろう。セイバーの言うことはもっともだけど、俺はもっと単純だと思うよ。
十年前さ、ここで切嗣に助けられた時はただ嬉しかった。それ以外になかったから、自分もそうなれたらいいと憧れたんじゃないかな」

pages.en:
“…I don't know. What you're saying makes sense, Saber, but I think my reason is simpler.

“Ten years ago, when Kiritsugu saved me here, I was just happy. There was nothing else inside me. I think I admired what he did because I wanted to become someone who could give another person that feeling.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I don’t know. What you say is true, but I think it’s simpler than that.
I was just happy when Kiritsugu saved me here ten years ago. There was nothing else, so maybe I admired him and wanted to be like him.”

pages.ja:
そう、ただ嬉しかった。
助けを求めて、それが叶えられた時の感情は言葉では言い表せない。
だが、同時に。
嬉しければ嬉しいほど、後ろめたさもあったのだ。

Yes. I was simply happy.

There are no words for what it feels like to beg for salvation and have your wish come true.

But at the same time—

The happier I was, the guiltier I felt.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s right, I was just happy at that time.
I can’t put into words the emotion I felt when my request for help was granted.
But at the same time.
The happier I was, the guiltier I felt.

pages.ja: 「けど、自分だけ願いが叶えられたってのは居心地が悪かった。俺は親父に助けられたけど。他の人たちは、助けられずにずっとこのままだ」
pages.jaRuby: 「けど、自分だけ願いが叶えられたってのは居心地が悪かった。俺は親父に助けられたけど。他の人たちは、助けられずにずっとこのままだ」
pages.en: “But knowing mine was the only wish that came true never sat right with me. My dad saved me. No one else was saved. They're still here, just as they were.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “But I didn’t feel at ease because I was the only one saved. I was saved by my father, but no one else was saved and ended up like this.”

pages.ja:
誰もが救いを求め、その中でただ一人、俺は願いを叶えられた。
ただ一人助かって、
他の全員を犠牲にして救われた。
だから
衛宮士郎は、その責任をとらなければ。

pages.en:
Everyone had prayed to be saved, and of them all, only my wish was granted.

I alone survived.

I was saved at everyone else's expense.

Therefore—Shirou Emiya has to bear the responsibility.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Everyone wished for help, and I was the only one who received it.
Only I was saved.
And I was saved with the sacrifice of everyone else.
SoEmiya Shirou must take responsibility for it.

「けどまあ、起きてしまった事は戻しようがないからな。
死んでいった人たちに報いたいなら、せめてこれからの事を防ぐべきだ。
十年前のような惨事は起こさせない。またあんな事になったら、それこそ犠牲になった人たちに会わせる顔がないだろ。
まあ、俺の理由なんてその程度のものだと思う」

pages.en:
“But nothing can undo what's already happened.

“If I want to honor the people who died, then the least I can do is stop it from happening again.

“I won't let there be another disaster like the one ten years ago. If I did, I could never face the people who died here.

“That's about all there is to my reason.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“But there’s no way to take back something that’s already happened.
If I want retribution for those that died, I should prevent what is to come.
I won’t allow a disaster like the one ten years ago to repeat itself. I couldn’t face the victims if that happens.
Well, I think my motive is something like that.”

そんな事より慎二捜しを再開しないと。
体調も良くなったし、まだ調べていないビルを急いで回らなければ。
それに、夜になれば人目も少なくなる。
慎二が俺たちを襲いたいのなら絶好の機会だろう。
自分たちを囮にするのなら、ここからが本番だ。

More importantly, we have to resume the search for Shinji.

I feel better now, and we need to hurry through the buildings we have not checked yet.

There will be fewer people around after dark.

If Shinji wants to attack us, this is his perfect chance.

If we mean to use ourselves as bait, this is where the real work begins.
pages.mirrorMoon:
More importantly, we should continue searching for Shinji.
I feel better, so we should go to the buildings we haven’t searched yet.
And there’ll be fewer people around at night.
If Shinji wants to attack us, now would be a perfect time.
If we are going to make ourselves a decoy, the real deal starts now.

“?”

“You said the same thing yesterday. I had sensed it before, but in that moment I became certain.

“—You have no intention of saving yourself.”

She looks me straight in the eye and pronounces it as though naming a sin.

“You said the same thing yesterday. I have felt it for a while, but I became confident about it then…
That you have no intention of saving yourself.”
As if…
…Even stating that fact is a crime, she stares at me and declares so.

“You place others before yourself. That is admirable, but one day it will surely bring you regret.

“…You must value yourself more, Shirou.”

Saber walks right past me.

“You are putting others ahead of yourself. That is admirable, but you will regret it someday if you continue like that.
…You should value yourself more, Shirou.”
Saber walks past me.

“Let us go. You are right—remaining here will only put you under further strain.”

Saber starts toward the office district.
